title: Conditions of Cancellation for a Keyturn Trip Booking
content:
A Keyturn Trip Booking reservation can be ended before the trip starts by the guest, by the host or by the marketplace, and who ended it decides entirely what money moves.

**When a fee is due.** A cancellation fee is raised only where the guest gives notice of the cancellation after the free cancellation window has elapsed, counted forward from the confirmation of the reservation. The free cancellation window is counted in whole elapsed hours from the timestamp of confirmation rather than in calendar days, and the window is exhausted only once the last hour has fully elapsed, so notice given exactly at the boundary is still free.

**What the fee comes to.** Where a fee is due it is a percentage of one locked daily rate plus the plan's flat component, and it never exceeds the plan's cancellation cap; the flat component is added to the percentage rather than taken as the higher of the two.

**No-show.** A guest who never appears is treated as a no-show once the plan's no-show grace has run from the scheduled start, and the no-show fee replaces the cancellation fee rather than being charged alongside it.

**Cancellation by the other side.** A cancellation by the host or by the marketplace raises no fee on the guest whatever the notice given; instead the guest is credited the plan's rebooking percentage of the trip price, and the credit lapses after the plan's validity period counted from the day it is issued.

**The trip fee.** The marketplace trip fee follows the base rate: it is returned in full where the cancellation is free and kept in full where a cancellation fee is due, and it is never partly returned.

**Effect on the calendar.** Ending the reservation releases the reserved hours back to the host's calendar on the same day, and a reservation already in progress is never cancelled but returned early instead.

### Who ended it, and what follows

| Ended by | Fee on the guest | Credit to the guest |
|---|---|---|
| The guest, inside the free window | None. | None; the marketplace trip fee is returned in full. |
| The guest, after the free window | A percentage of one locked daily rate plus the flat component, held to the cap. | None; the marketplace trip fee is kept in full. |
| The guest, who never appears, after the no-show grace | The no-show fee, in place of the cancellation fee. | None. |
| The host | None, whatever the notice given. | The plan's rebooking percentage of the trip price. |
| The marketplace | None, whatever the notice given. | The plan's rebooking percentage of the trip price. |

Who ended the reservation is recorded on the reservation itself alongside its reference number and the guest it belongs to. It is the one condition here settled partly on what the parties state rather than on the records alone, and it is established before the reservation is ended.

### The free window at its boundary

The clock starts at the timestamp of confirmation and runs forward by the hours the plan carries, counted as whole elapsed hours and never converted into calendar days.

- *Hypothetical, on a plan whose free window is 24 hours.* Confirmation at 14:00 on the boundary day, notice given at 14:00 the following day — exactly 24 whole hours later. The window is exhausted only once the last hour has fully elapsed, so notice at that exact moment is still free and no fee is raised.
- *Hypothetical, same plan.* Notice given at 14:30 the following day. The window has elapsed and the notice falls after it, so a cancellation fee is due.

### The fee, worked through

*Hypothetical inputs: a locked daily rate of 120.00 USD, on a plan whose percentage is 25 per cent, whose flat component is 9.50 USD and whose cap is 45.00 USD.*

Twenty-five per cent of one locked daily rate is 30.00 USD. The flat component of 9.50 USD is added to it, not weighed against it, giving 39.50 USD, which is below the cap of 45.00 USD and is therefore the fee. Had the two together come to more than 45.00 USD, the cap of 45.00 USD would have been charged.
